summary: Extend the parent’s modular-curve direction to integral genus-two Siegel forms, arbitrary torsion coefficients and K/O. Nine layers give the all-component Fourier interface, primary and secondary Hasse geometry, coefficient operators and corrected Q₂, integral geometric Hecke actions, characteristic-p theta and ordinary full-frame comparison. Existing bundle, BT₁, compactification and primary-Hasse owners are imported. This is a completed planning pass with precise open supplier requests and six mathematical verification gaps; it is not a closed or implemented roadmap. The independent generic GL₃ direction is proposed as a separate roadmap.

nodes.title: Integral Siegel forms and cusp forms
nodes.statement: Fix neat tame level K^p and hyperspecial level at p. On the imported smooth toroidal Siegel threefold X over O, let E=e*Ω¹_G/X and λ=det E. For integers j≥k put ω(j,k)=Sym^(j−k)E⊗λ^k and ω(j,k)^sub=ω(j,k)⊗I_D, using the imported bundles. For every O-module M define M_(j,k)(M)=H⁰(X,ω(j,k)⊗_O M) and S_(j,k)(M)=H⁰(X,ω(j,k)^sub⊗_O M). All components are retained. Ω(d,r)=ω(d+r,r). The notation H⁰ with M=K/O means the sheaf tensor product, not a tensor of H⁰ with K/O.
hypotheses: O is a complete DVR finite over Z_p, uniformizer ϖ, fraction field K and residue field k₀.
A good projective smooth cone decomposition is chosen; tame auxiliary covers are finite étale.

nodes.title: Integral q-expansion principle
nodes.statement: The family of expansion maps on one cusp of each geometric connected component is injective for every O-module M. For M=O, a rational section of ω(j,k) or its subcanonical extension whose coefficients at all these cusps are integral belongs to the integral global-section lattice. More generally, divisibility of an integral section by ϖ^m is equivalent to divisibility of all its coefficients. This is a statement about sections and their saturated lattice, not a surjectivity assertion for arbitrary formal series.
hypotheses: The models and coefficient transports are those of S1.
Use all relevant components after the tame cyclotomic extension.
proofSteps: Apply Tilouine Proposition 3.2 on each geometrically connected good-level model and descend along the faithfully flat coefficient extension.
For O/ϖ^m use the same chart argument with arbitrary coefficients, then use injectivity of reduction to test divisibility.
Clear denominators of a rational section, lower their exponent using mod-ϖ injectivity, and repeat.

nodes.title: Simple Hasse zeros at rank one
nodes.statement: The nonordinary zero schemes S and S_par are reduced effective Cartier divisors. In the rank-one crystalline basis e₁,e₂,e₃,e₄ with F e₁=p e₁, F e₂=−p e₃, F e₃=e₂ and F e₄=e₄, choose the alternating pairing with ⟨e₁,e₄⟩=⟨e₂,e₃⟩=1. A first-order Hodge lift generated by columns (1,0,X,W) and (0,1,Y,Z) has Hasse linear term −Y. The principal tangent equation X=Z, and the two paramodular equations Z=0 and X=0, leave Y free. Thus h vanishes simply at every generic point of the nonordinary divisor. Normality of the ambient special fiber and Cohen–Macaulayness give reducedness globally.

nodes.title: Hasse expansion and multiplication
nodes.statement: At every split cusp the imported primary Hasse section has Fourier expansion 1. It is a nonzerodivisor on X₁ because the ordinary locus is dense on every component. The determinant Hasse ideal used on an integral Hilbert modular chart is locally (p,h) after specializing the same semiabelian determinant, with its chosen Hodge trivialization; it is not a different invariant.

nodes.title: Secondary Hasse invariant on rank one
nodes.statement: Over a reduced F_p-scheme B let G be a height-four, dimension-two BT₁ with constant multiplicative and étale ranks both one. Import G^m⊂G^o⊂G and put G^oo=G^o/G^m. Define h′(G)=Ha(G^m)^(p+1)⊗h′(G^oo) in (det ω_G)^(p²−1). It is a unit on B. The same recipe applies to the connected height-three, dimension-two BT₁ with multiplicative rank one and biconnected quotient of height two, to handle the boundary; its duality claim is only made in the height-four case.

nodes.title: Canonical subgroup in the Frobenius kernel
nodes.statement: Let B be reduced normal, G a height-four dimension-two BT₁, generically of multiplicative and étale ranks one, and suppose ker(V*:ω_G→ω_G^(p)) is an invertible direct summand. Apply the same construction to G^D to obtain L. Let N=ω_(G[F]/H) and N_D=ω_(G^D[F]/L). The Hodge diagram defines V_H*:ω_H→ω_H^p, W:N^p→coker(V*), and Z:N_D^∨→coker(V*); all three are maps between line bundles. The source of Z uses coker(F*)≅N_D^∨; Z is an isomorphism, since the full crystalline V* has image ω_G^(p) and kernel im F*.

nodes.title: Normal-base extension of secondary Hasse
nodes.statement: Under the preceding normal-base hypotheses, h′ extends uniquely across B. Its support of zeros is the complement of the open where both multiplicative and étale ranks are one. Their product, under LF and determinant identifications, extends (h′)². Normality then extends the rational section h′ itself. If the two ranks agree at every point, both individual zero-locus descriptions reduce to the same rank-zero set.

Its coefficient realization retains, for each contributing M and its transformed representative P, the intertwiner ρ_d(M): a(ZF,Q)=Σ_Mρ_d(M)a(F,P). nodes.statement: Restrict the imported compactified C_(p,2) isogeny correspondence (Pilloni indexing; CG20 β₁) to the formal locus X^{≥1}. Both relevant projections are proper and quasi-finite, hence finite, and are generically étale. In the interior they classify isotropic Lagrangian rank-p² kernels. At a geometric ordinary or rank-one point, only finitely many such subgroups occur; positive-dimensional families of α_p-subgroups arise only on the excluded rank-zero locus. At the boundary use the imported degeneration chart. This is a restriction of the existing correspondence, not a new Hilbert-scheme construction.

nodes.title: Ordinary trace divisibility
nodes.statement: For the finite correspondence over X^{≥1}, write d=j−k≥0 and r=k≥2. On the formal neighborhood of an ordinary point the kernel types are multiplicative, mixed and étale. The differential on Ω(d,r) factors respectively through p^(d+2r), p^r and 1; the trace factors respectively through 1, p and p³. Thus the raw pullback followed by trace lands in p³Ω(d,r), including the subcanonical boundary twist. For r=2 these are the source’s p^(d+4),p²,1 differential bounds. The trace bounds are ideals/divisibility statements, not merely the degrees of maps.

The bound on the symmetric-power part in the mixed case is only integrality; it is not assumed divisible by p^d.

For a mixed kernel use a basis with differential diag(p,1), yielding the determinant factor p^r and an integral symmetric-power map.
For an étale kernel the differential is an isomorphism; compute trace ideals in Serre–Tate coordinates as p and p³ for the ramified covers.
Each product has p-order at least three when r≥2. The source’s r=2 computation is extended by the stated determinant factors.

nodes.title: Integral paramodular composite correspondence
nodes.statement: Write d=j−k≥0 and r=k≥2. On the imported spherical, Klingen and paramodular lci models, form the degree-p³ and degree-p isogeny correspondences. Their differential maps tensored with fundamental classes have integral factorizations by p^(r+2) and p respectively. Normalize these integral maps before passing to coefficients, then compose to obtain C_r on integral coherent cohomology. Rationally, in the CG20 normalization, C_r=p^(3−r)(T₂+(1+p+p²+p³)S). In the trivial central sector Q₂=C_r−(1+p²)p^(j−2)·1. This difference is integral for every j≥k≥2, and its finite-coefficient and K/O actions are obtained from the integral derived correspondence, without lifting torsion sections. Here C_r is Pilloni’s operator T in §7; it is distinct from CG20 T and from either source’s individual numbered generators.
hypotheses: The models, maps, normality and lci hypotheses are imported from C14; the fundamental class and trace require the exact DUAL request.

The composite double coset has one noncentral component β₂, and the central component has multiplicity 1+p+p²+p³, the number of Klingen lines. With the total normalization p^(−r−3), this gives the stated rational C_r.
Subtract (1+p²)p^(j−2), since p^(3−r)S=p^(j−3), to obtain exactly the S5 cancelled Q₂ formula. Reduce the integral derived maps only after their construction.
